body:
kobo.py:1236-1243 (embedded-state branch) advances new_reading_state_last_modified to the max of every reading state embedded in the page's books; the standalone loop at :1465 is ordered ascending and capped at SYNC_ITEM_LIMIT=100; :1687 writes the max of both to the token. Any KoboReadingState whose last_modified falls between the 100th standalone row and the embedded max is skipped and the cursor closes over it forever — when that book's entitlement later arrives, the embed condition (krs.last_modified > sync_token.reading_state_last_modified) is false, so it arrives stateless.

Trigger: any sync with >100 states newer than the cursor plus one recently-read book in the current page. Canonical case is the recovery scenario itself: factory-reset device on a several-hundred-book library (KoboSyncedBooks-empty branch at :782 resets the cursor to datetime.min, making every state pending). Damage: device silently never receives progress/read-status for skipped books; a device-side open can then push a 0%/low state back.

CONFIDENCE: mechanism OBSERVED in code (verified independently of the audit agent, 2026-09-01). Hardware effect likely. Settle with an integration test: 250 books with states, fresh token, walk all pages, count states delivered vs stored. Source: adversarial audit state/kobo-audit-2026-09-01.
title: Reading-state cursor advances past states the capped loop never emitted; fresh-device sync permanently withholds positions on large libraries
